newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open weaker as currency softens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open weaker as currency softens.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened softer on Monday as weakness in the Canadian dollar helped push prices lower in quiet trade, dealers said.

"It's really currency related I would say. The U.S. dollar is off significantly against the yen and there's currency concerns," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "It's quite light at the start here."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 2.97 percent from 2.96 percent at the close of trading on Friday.
Canada's dollar opened weaker at C$1.3860 (US$0.7215) in light trading on Monday after the Japanese yen made steady overnight gains against the U.S. dollar in overseas markets, traders said.

Canadian housing starts and capacity utilization data out this morning were largely in line with expectations and had little impact on the money market, dealers said. Analysts said there would be no major Canadian or U.S. economic data released in the early part of this week.
"I think we'll probably just trade in a bit of a range here for the time being," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.31 percent from 3.29 percent. The one-year T-bill softened to yield 3.78 percent from 3.73 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 2.95 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
